title: manni lint config section
description: The `lint:` section of a shared `manni.config.yaml`. The file's root is a mapping of tool name to that tool's settings, so this schema describes the section only - never the file. The document set is not here: proposal 0041 declares it once for every tool, under the family-level `collections:` key, and `paths`/`exclude` under `lint:` are refused by name. Every key is optional: a repo that configures no manni lint at all is a legitimate config, and so is one that carries only a sibling tool's section. `additionalProperties: false` applies at every level below `lint:`, which is what turns a typo'd key into a loud failure instead of a silent default.

allowEmpty.description: Treat a run that matched zero files as a success rather than an operational error. The same key, with the same meaning, as `cite.allowEmpty`: for a shared CI template or a pre-commit hook whose file list may legitimately be empty. `--allow-empty` on the command line sets it for one run.

overrides.description: Repo policy: everything under a glob is linted with one template, whatever the pages say they are. First matching entry wins, and an override outranks a page's own `type`.

items.description: One policy entry. Both keys are required: an entry naming no template, or no files, is a line that silently does nothing.

files.description: Glob matched against each file's path, written with forward slashes whatever the platform uses.

template.description: Template ref applied to the files this entry matches.

structure.description: The structure job, which `manni lint structure` and `manni lint check` both run. Declaring it with no keys is how a repo says the job applies. Its one setting is the tool that performs it.

tool.description: Which tool performs the job. `manni` is manni's own template-structure engine; `dita-ot` is DITA Open Toolkit, which validates a DITA map and the topics it reaches and is located through the top-level `tools.dita-ot.home`. `--tool <name>` on the command line names the same thing.

template.description: Template ref applied to a page that declares no doctype and matches no override. The last stage of the resolution chain, not an override: `--template`, a page's `$template`, an `overrides` entry, and the page's own `type` all outrank it.

templates.description: Template files to load. Their templates' `types:` join the doctype routing table, outranking the built-ins, so adopting a repo's own how-to shape is one entry here and no flag.

types.description: Explicit doctype -> template ref map, for a doctype no template file claims with its own `types:`. Keys are the vocabulary a page's `type` frontmatter is written in, so they are the author's names rather than this schema's - constrained only to the shape a doctype slug takes, not to a fixed set.

^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$.description: A template ref: a built-in id, a path, or a URL, optionally with a `#name` fragment.
